info.blurb: A0620-00 (V616 Monocerotis) is one of the closest known stellar-mass black holes, discovered during a huge 1975 X-ray flare.
info.funFact: It is roughly 3 to 5 times the Sun's mass and about 1,000 parsecs away.

info.blurb: Cygnus X-1 was the first source widely accepted as a stellar-mass black hole. It pulls gas from a blue supergiant companion, heating it until it blazes in X-rays.
info.funFact: Its 1974 bet with Stephen Hawking (who conceded in 1990) made it the most famous black hole.

info.blurb: GRS 1915+105 hosts a black hole that fires jets of plasma apparently faster than light (an illusion of relativistic beaming), the first such 'microquasar' seen in the Milky Way.
info.funFact: Its jets appear to move at 1.25 times light speed due to relativistic beaming.

info.blurb: Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, about 4.3 million times the mass of the Sun. It was imaged in 2022 by the Event Horizon Telescope.
info.funFact: Sgr A* is the closest supermassive black hole; its shadow is the target of the 2022 EHT image.

info.blurb: V404 Cygni is a black hole that siphons gas from a companion star, erupting into spectacular X-ray outbursts such as the famous 2015 event.
info.funFact: During its 2015 outburst it became briefly the brightest X-ray source in the sky.

info.blurb: The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest large galaxy and the most distant object visible to the unaided eye, heading toward us for a future merger with the Milky Way.
info.funFact: It will collide and merge with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years.
